newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swissair head says won't abandon Sabena.
newsitem.headline: Swissair head says won't abandon Sabena.

text.p: Philippe Bruggisser, chief operating officer of Swissair AG, said on Sunday that he was not planning to abandon partner Belgian carrier Sabena, despite recent threats of such a move.
"A withdrawal from Sabena is not an issue," Bruggisser said in an interview with Swiss Sunday newspaper Sonntags Zeitung.
Bruggisser's support for Sabena is significant because he was one of the few Swissair executives that had opposed the acquisition of a 49.5 percent stake in Sabena last year.
"The Sabena engagement is not a disappointment, we are on target," Bruggisser said.
Bruggisser also said 10 percent of the expected savings of 60 million Swiss francs ($47 million) in 1997 from the cooperation between Swissair and Sabena had been achieved.

In the first half of 1996 Sabena lost two billion Belgian francs ($64 million) and has been suffering as a result of a series of strikes in February. In 1995 Sabena reported a group loss before provisions of 530 million Belgian francs compared with a 1.23 billion franc loss in 1994.

Last week Sabena's chief executive officer, Paul Reutlinger, previously head of marketing at Swissair, said Swissair was considering writing off its investment in Sabena and this would give it the freedom to walk away from Sabena.
Swissair spokesmen have said there are no plans to pull out of Sabena even if Swissair decides to write-off its stake in Sabena, valued at around 250 million Swiss francs.

Reutlinger's threat came after announcing a draft deal with four Belgian trade union on a 4.7 billion Belgian francs recovery plan for Sabena. The deal is part of his plan to turn around Sabena and make it break even in 1998.
Sabena pilots, which had gone on strike to protest the deal, were later convinced to end the strike.
Swissair's profitability so far this year is slightly better than last year, a performance that is "probably somewhat worse than expected," Bruggisser also told the Sonntags Zeitung.
In the first half of 1996 Swissair reported a group net loss of 51 million francs, down from 86 million the year before. Losses in the first half of the year are quite normal.
For the full year Swissair expects to report a profit compared with 1995's net loss of 147 million francs, largely due to extraordinary restructuring charges of 365 million.
-- Peter Nielsen, Zurich Editorial +41 1 631 7340 ($1=1.2700 Swiss Franc, $1=31.27 Belgian Franc)
